svg.title: P030 | Repeat versus one-time customers
svg.desc: Four orders become three customers and two report rows. A separate fifth order with a missing customer ID shows the effect of the filter.
svg.text: Follow customer 20 from two orders to one member of the Repeat group.
Blue cells track Orders. The triangle marks the row to follow. The ƒ symbol marks a calculated field.

g.text: Orders supplies both IDs. WHERE CustomerID IS NOT NULL keeps orders that can be assigned to a customer. All
Orders 2 and 3 both belong to customer 20.

g.aria-label: Why count orders per customer first?
g.text: Why count orders per customer first?
GROUP BY CustomerID puts each customer’s orders together. COUNT(OrderID) counts the order IDs in each
4 eligible orders become 3 customer rows. Customer 20 has 2 orders.

g.aria-label: Which label does each customer receive?
g.text: Which label does each customer receive?
CASE gives One-time to a count of 1 and Repeat to a count of 2 or more. Each customer keeps one CTE row.
Customer 20 receives Repeat. Customers 10 and 30 each receive One-time.

g.aria-label: What does the outer COUNT count?
g.text: What does the outer COUNT count?
FROM customer_order_counts supplies three customers. GROUP BY customer_type brings customers with the
COUNT(total_orders) sees two values in One-time and one value in Repeat. Customer 20 contributes one

g.aria-label: Which customers belong in the denominator?
g.text: Which customers belong in the denominator?
The scalar subquery counts all 3 CTE rows. One-time is 2 ÷ 3 × 100 = 66.67%. Repeat is 1 ÷ 3 × 100 =
The report accounts for 2 + 1 = 3 customers. Its two displayed shares add to 100.00%.

g.aria-label: What happens to an order with no customer ID?
g.text: What happens to an order with no customer ID?
Start again from the original four orders and add order 5. In the submitted query its NULL group has one order

g.aria-label: Fifth order added for this check
g.data-table: Fifth order added for this check
g.text: Fifth order added for this check

g.aria-label: Report with the same fifth order
g.data-table: Report with the same fifth order
g.text: Report with the same fifth order
The revised CTE filters order 5 before grouping. Its denominator stays at 3 identified customers.
